claim: The reproduced LoFi editor-removal crash loses an unconsumed audio request; selecting the existing per-process UI Automation workaround on the exact LoFi registration prevents that measured crash in matched cold-start close/reopen and musical use.
clock_rule: Windows QPC and Linux monotonic are separate; no cross-domain subtraction.

causal_baseline.condition: Fresh bridge owner/environment after prior clean shutdown; normally Applications-launched Bitwig; saved pair; transport stopped; real LoFi editor close.
causal_baseline.interpretation: UI owner is inside IPlugView::removed (view stage 212). Previous audio request 12737 completed; request 12738 is published but not consumed. The host disappears before the unchanged five-second reply timeout. This is process loss during editor teardown, not a five-second vendor DSP computation.
limitations: No complete vendor call stack was captured.
The original operator failure at position 823296 lacked this status and is not retrospectively proven to have this cause.

A warm unmodified close also succeeded when UI Automation was not mapped; that retry is not the repair. Xalia/runtime activation explains a possible loading difference, but its precise trigger is unproved.

repair_check.limitation: Windows UI Automation/screen-reader integration is disabled for these selected processes. VST parameter automation remains active. No global override, runtime/vendor replacement or timeout/buffer change.
